## Description

A volvocine green alga (10–50 µm) inside a large gelatinous envelope crossed by its two flagella, with
an eyespot; it lives in rock pools and bird baths. Under stress (strong light, lack of nitrogen) it
encysts and turns blood red with astaxanthin (aplanospores).

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 4 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A [stress pigment](../../mechanics/metabolism-and-nutrients.md): with light above the threshold or without N it
accumulates astaxanthin in lipid droplets (twice as fast in the cyst) over days; the pigment filters
light and protects from [photo-oxidative damage](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md#phototaxis-photophobia-and-light-damage),
while the green cell suffers under intense light. Rates and thresholds estimated from that time
course.

## Not implemented yet

- No measured µmax in the data.
- The cyst does not survive desiccation of the plate (there is no drying).

## Unique and shared mechanics

The stress pigment is unique to it; shares phototaxis with the flagellated phototrophs and light
damage with *Blepharisma*.
